# Config Schema

Alpage config is HCL. The blocks below are the complete schema; it is generated from the `hcl:"..."` struct tags in `nns/`, so it always matches what the tool parses.

This page documents the current development schema, ahead of the latest release. The Since column gives the release each block and field first appeared in, so a field newer than your binary is visible as such; see [Schema History](#schema-history) for the schema as of each release.

## `resources.hcl`

### `subnet "<name>" { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> A subnet, referenced from proposals and nodes as `subnet.<name>.id`.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Principal of the subnet. |
| `label` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Human-readable name. |
| `sev_enabled` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.1">v0.1.1</span> | Whether the subnet runs with SEV-SNP enabled, reconciled against the registry's features.sev_enabled. Omitted means false. |
| `type` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.2.0">v0.2.0</span> | Subnet type: application, verified_application, system, or cloud_engine. Omitted means application. |
| `cost_schedule` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.2.0">v0.2.0</span> | Canister cycles cost schedule: normal or free. Omitted means free for a cloud_engine, which the registry requires, and normal otherwise. |
| `admins` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.2.0">v0.2.0</span> | Principals with admin rights on the subnet (subnet_admins). Allowed only on a cloud_engine or a rented subnet (application on the free schedule), at most 10. Declaring none asserts none, so an admin added on-chain is drift. Order is not significant. |

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> A node provider, referenced by node_operator as `node_provider.<name>.id`.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Principal of the node provider. |
| `label` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Human-readable name. |

Its block is kept so historical proposal payloads keep resolving to the ids they were submitted with; reconcile expects it, and every operator under it, to be absent from the registry. |

### `node_operator "<name>" { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> A node operator, referenced by node as `node_operator.<name>.id`.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Principal of the node operator. |
| `label` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Human-readable name. |
| `provider` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Id of its node provider (`node_provider.<name>.id`). |
| `dc` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Id of its data center (`data_center.<name>.id`). |
| `decommissioned` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Marks a node operator removed on-chain. Its block is kept so historical proposal payloads keep resolving to the ids they were submitted with; reconcile expects it to be absent from the registry. Implied for every operator under a decommissioned node_provider. |

### `guestos_version "<name>" { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.3.0">v0.3.0</span> A named GuestOS/replica version, referenced by node and by deploy_guestos as `guestos_version.<name>.id`. `alp guestos sync` generates the elected set as resources/guestos.hcl.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.3.0">v0.3.0</span> | GuestOS/replica version hash. Spelled id, not hash, so it resolves through the same `<kind>.<name>.id` form as every other resource. |
| `label` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.3.0">v0.3.0</span> | Human-readable name (e.g. the release name). |
| `default` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Marks the version every node is expected to run unless its own block overrides it, so a fleet-wide rollout is one edit here rather than one per node. At most one guestos_version may carry it; two is a load error. With a default declared, a node omitting guestos_version inherits it instead of going unchecked, so `guestos_version = "none"` is how a single node opts out. |

### `node "<name>" { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> A node, referenced from proposals as `node.<name>.id`.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Principal of the node. |
| `label` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Human-readable name. |
| `subnet` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Id of the subnet it belongs to (`subnet.<name>.id`). Empty means unassigned. |
| `operator` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Id of its node operator (`node_operator.<name>.id`). |
| `decommissioned` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.1">v0.1.1</span> | Marks a node deregistered on-chain. Its block is kept so historical proposal payloads keep resolving to the ids they were submitted with; reconcile expects it to be absent from the registry. |
| `guestos_version` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.2.0">v0.2.0</span> | GuestOS/replica version this node is expected to run. Not a registry fact: the registry stores one version per subnet, so reconcile reads the node's own /api/v2/status impl_version, which needs IPv6. If the node is unreachable it falls back to the public dashboard, marking the row "via dashboard" since that data may lag. Reconcile also checks the version against the NNS elected set and marks it "NOT ELECTED" if absent; when that source is unreadable the check is skipped rather than failing. Omitted inherits the guestos_version marked default, and means unchecked when there is none; setting it while a default exists marks the row "[override]". "none" opts the node out of the check entirely. |
| `chip_id` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.4.0">v0.4.0</span> | The node's AMD SEV-SNP CHIP_ID as hex, the form AMD's KDS takes as its hwID parameter (base64 is also accepted; comparison is on the decoded bytes). 64 opaque bytes identifying the physical CPU, recorded by the registry canister only for a node onboarded with SEV. Pins hardware identity, not live TEE state. Reconcile also asks AMD KDS to vouch for the chip, caching the verdict in state.json. Omitted asserts the node carries none, so gaining, losing, or changing one is drift; an unread record reports "unknown". |

## `proposals.hcl`

### `provider { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> Global submission settings; CLI flags override these.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `host` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Governance host URL. Defaults per command; overridden by `--host`. |
| `neuron` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Proposer neuron id. |
| `fetch_root_key` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Whether to fetch the IC root key. Unset defaults to true for non-mainnet hosts. |

### `proposal "<name>" { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> One NNS proposal. Carries common metadata plus a nested block named after its kind.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `kind` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Proposal kind; selects the nested block (membership, deploy_guestos, update_subnet, remove_nodes, remove_node_operators, remove_node_provider, add_data_centers, add_node_provider, add_node_operator). |
| `title` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Proposal title shown on the NNS. |
| `summary` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Proposal summary (markdown). |
| `url` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Reference URL (e.g. forum thread). |

### `membership { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.3.0">v0.3.0</span> Nested in a proposal of kind "membership": change_subnet_membership. Holds add/remove [node](#node-) blocks. Renamed from resize in v0.3.0; a config written for v0.2.0 or earlier must rename the block and its kind.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `subnet_id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.3.0">v0.3.0</span> | Subnet whose membership changes (`subnet.<name>.id`). |
| `add` | block | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.3.0">v0.3.0</span> | A node to add to the subnet; repeatable. See the [add / remove](#add-remove-) block. |
| `remove` | block | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.3.0">v0.3.0</span> | A node to remove from the subnet; repeatable. See the [add / remove](#add-remove-) block. |

### `deploy_guestos { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> Nested in a proposal of kind "deploy_guestos": deploy_guestos_to_all_subnet_nodes.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `subnet_id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Subnet whose nodes to upgrade (`subnet.<name>.id`). |
| `replica_version_id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Replica version to deploy to every node in the subnet (`guestos_version.<name>.id`, or the hash itself). Must be elected by the NNS: preflight checks the registry for a `replica_version_<id>` record (read via the registry explorer) and refuses an unelected version, since the NNS would reject the proposal. `--force` submits anyway, and also lets apply proceed when that lookup fails (downgraded to a warning); plan always degrades that way. Preflight additionally resolves the version's release name and election proposal from the public dashboard, which is display-only and degrades to a note when unavailable. |

### `update_subnet { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Nested in a proposal of kind "update_subnet": update_subnet (UPDATE_CONFIG_OF_SUBNET). Changes a subnet's configuration record. Every field is optional and an omitted one is left untouched on-chain, so a proposal changes exactly what it declares. Preflight diffs every declared field against the current record. Two payload fields are not ordinary settings here: subnet_type, which the registry asserts is unchanged, and sev_enabled, which the registry refuses to turn off.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `subnet_id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Subnet whose configuration changes (`subnet.<name>.id`). |
| `is_halted` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Whether the subnet is halted: a halted subnet no longer creates or executes blocks. This is how a subnet is frozen for a recovery, and setting it back to false is how it resumes. |
| `halt_at_cup_height` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Halt the subnet once it reaches the next CUP height rather than immediately, so it stops at a known state. The registry resets this flag when a new CUP proposal is approved and sets is_halted instead, so the subnet stays halted until a later proposal sets is_halted = false. |
| `max_number_of_canisters` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Maximum number of canisters that may be present on the subnet at any one time. 0 does not mean unlimited: it means the replica's own default applies. |
| `ssh_readonly_access` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Public keys whose owners get "readonly" SSH access to every replica on the subnet, for when a subnet recovery has to be performed. The list is replaced, not merged, so it must name every key that keeps access; an empty list revokes all of them. Preflight flags a declared list that clears existing entries. |
| `ssh_backup_access` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Public keys whose owners get "backup" SSH access to the subnet's nodes, which is what makes backing up the NNS possible. Replaced wholesale like ssh_readonly_access. |
| `subnet_admins` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Principals that have admin privileges on the subnet. Replaced wholesale, so the list must be complete. |
| `features` | block | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | The subnet's feature flags. Replaced wholesale; see the [features](#features-) block. |
| `resource_limits` | block | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | The subnet's resource-consumption limits. Replaced wholesale; see the [resource_limits](#resource_limits-) block. |
| `unit_delay_millis` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Unit delay for the blockmaker, in milliseconds. |
| `initial_notary_delay_millis` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Initial delay for the notary, in milliseconds, which gives rank-0 blocks time to propagate. |
| `dkg_interval_length` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Length of every DKG interval, counted in the rounds that follow the DKG summary. |
| `dkg_dealings_per_block` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Upper bound on the number of DKG dealings allowed in one block. |
| `max_ingress_bytes_per_message` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Maximum bytes per ingress message. A hard cap: a message over the limit is dropped. |
| `max_ingress_bytes_per_block` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | How big an ingress payload may be when held in memory, which may exceed max_block_payload_size since ingress messages are stripped before a block is disseminated. 0 means the replica's built-in default; too high a value drives up replica memory use. |
| `max_ingress_messages_per_block` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Maximum number of ingress messages per block. |
| `max_block_payload_size` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Maximum size in bytes a block payload may have when sent over the wire. Setting it too high slows block delivery to peers, which can cause forks as higher-rank blocks get proposed meanwhile. |

### `remove_nodes { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Nested in a proposal of kind "remove_nodes": deregisters nodes, freeing their operators' allowance. Holds one [node](#node-) block per node. The registry rejects a node that is still a subnet member, so remove it from its subnet first; preflight checks this before the proposal is cut.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `node` | block | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | A node to deregister. Repeat the block for each one. |

### `remove_node_operators { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Nested in a proposal of kind "remove_node_operators": deletes node operator records. The registry silently skips an operator that still owns nodes, so deregister its nodes first; preflight checks this.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `operators` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Ids of the node operators whose records to delete (`node_operator.<name>.id`). |

### `remove_node_provider { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Nested in a proposal of kind "remove_node_provider": removes a node provider. Unlike the other kinds this is a native governance action rather than an ExecuteNnsFunction. Governance rejects a provider it does not know, and removing one that still has operators orphans them; preflight checks both.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `node_provider_id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Principal of the node provider to remove (`node_provider.<name>.id`). |

### `add_data_centers { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Nested in a proposal of kind "add_data_centers": registers data center records, one [dc](#dc-) block each. Only adds: the payload can also remove, but removal has its own preconditions and is not exposed here. The canister traps on a dc_id it already holds, and it drops a record whose id, region, or owner exceeds 255 bytes while still reporting the proposal as executed, so preflight checks both before the proposal is cut. Ids are lowercased on the way in, which alpage does up front so the payload matches the record that lands.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `dc` | block | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | A data center record to register, repeated once per data center. See the [dc](#dc-) block. |

### `add_node_provider { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Nested in a proposal of kind "add_node_provider": registers a node provider. A native governance action rather than an ExecuteNnsFunction. Governance rejects a principal that is already a provider; preflight checks that. The self-declaration is not part of the payload, which carries only the principal and an optional reward account, so link it from the proposal's url and summarise it in summary.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `node_provider_id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Principal of the node provider to register (`node_provider.<name>.id`). Governance rejects a principal it already knows. |
| `reward_account` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Ledger account identifier rewards are paid to, as 64 hex characters. Optional: governance pays a provider with no reward_account into the default account of the provider principal, and a later UpdateNodeProvider can redirect the rewards. Governance validates the embedded checksum, so alpage rejects a malformed one when the config loads. |

### `add_node_operator { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Nested in a proposal of kind "add_node_operator": registers a node operator under a provider, in a data center, with an allowance of nodes it may register. Submitted as ASSIGN_NOID, governance's name for the registry's add_node_operator. Both referents must already exist on-chain, which makes this the last of the three onboarding proposals. The data center and the provider do not depend on each other, so those two can go in either order or at once. Preflight checks the data center, the provider, and that the operator principal is still free.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `node_operator_id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Principal of the node operator to register (`node_operator.<name>.id`). The operator signs add_node with this identity, so it must be a principal they hold the key for. |
| `node_provider_id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Principal of the provider this operator belongs to (`node_provider.<name>.id`). Governance rejects the proposal at submission when the provider is not registered, so the add_node_provider proposal has to land first. |
| `dc_id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Data center the operator's nodes sit in (`data_center.<name>.id`). The node-operator invariant rejects an unknown one when the proposal executes, so the add_data_centers proposal has to land first. |
| `node_allowance` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | How many nodes the operator may register before another proposal raises it. Omitted means 0, which is expected for a Cloud Engine operator because it needs no allowance. Any other operator with a 0 allowance gets a working record that cannot yet add nodes, so preflight reports the value either way. |
| `ipv6` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | The operator's IPv6 prefix, recorded on the operator record. Omitting it leaves the field unset. |
| `max_rewardable_nodes` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Node reward type mapped to the maximum number of nodes of that type the provider may be rewarded for, e.g. { type3.1 = 28 }. Omitted means none of them, which is the case for an operator outside the node provider reward scheme. The payload's other reward map, rewardable_nodes, is the field the registry canister itself calls the old one, so alpage always sends it empty rather than exposing it. |

### `add / remove { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> Inside a [membership](#membership-) block: a node to add to or remove from the subnet.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Node id (`node.<name>.id`). |
| `label` | attr | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.1.0">v0.1.0</span> | Optional human-readable name. |

### `features { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Inside an [update_subnet](#update_subnet-) block: the subnet's feature flags. Sending it replaces the whole features record rather than merging, so all three fields are required: an omitted one would be written as false. sev_enabled must therefore restate what the subnet already has; the registry rejects a change to it.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `canister_sandboxing` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Whether canister execution happens in a sandboxed process. Disabled by default. |
| `http_requests` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Whether canisters on the subnet may perform outbound HTTP(S) requests. |
| `sev_enabled` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Whether the subnet runs with SEV-SNP enabled. Required because the features record is replaced wholesale, which is also the trap: omitting it reads as disabling SEV, and the registry refuses to disable it. Enabling it is allowed, but execution traps unless every node already carries a chip_id and the subnet's GuestOS version has launch measurements. Preflight blocks a disable and warns on an enable. |

### `resource_limits { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Inside an [update_subnet](#update_subnet-) block: the subnet's state-size limits. Replaced wholesale like features, so both fields are required.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `maximum_state_size` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Maximum subnet state size in bytes. |
| `maximum_state_delta` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Maximum subnet state delta in bytes. |

### `dc { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Inside an [add_data_centers](#add_data_centers-) block: one data center record to register. Repeat the block for each one. Distinct from the data_center resource block, which only names an existing id for reference; this one carries the fields the registry stores.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `id` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Registry data center id (`data_center.<name>.id`), at most 255 bytes and short by convention, e.g. zh3. The canister lowercases it, so alpage does too and the payload matches the record that lands. |
| `region` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Registry region string as comma-separated continent,country,city (e.g. Europe,CH,Zurich). Reference `data_center.<name>.region` so the resource block stays the single source. The node reward table is keyed by region prefix, so this decides what the data center's nodes can earn. |
| `owner` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Legal owner of the data center as the self-declaration names it. Free text the NNS displays, at most 255 bytes. |
| `gps` | block | no | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Optional coordinates for the site, described by the [gps](#gps-) block. Omitting the block leaves the record without them. |

### `gps { }`

<span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> Inside a [dc](#dc-) block: the site's coordinates. Optional, and omitted leaves the record without them.

| Field | Kind | Required | Since | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------|-------------|
| `latitude` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Latitude in decimal degrees, between -90 and 90. |
| `longitude` | attr | yes | <span class="since" title="Introduced in v0.5.0">v0.5.0</span> | Longitude in decimal degrees, between -180 and 180. |
